status: draft: unratified, not yet calibrated on real submissions
credential: AI Architect Credential (AI Architect Academy, design-reviewed)

scale.0: Absent. The artifact or behaviour is missing.
scale.1: Asserted. Present as a claim, but the evidence cannot be re-derived from the submission alone.
scale.2: Partial. Real and re-derivable, with a gap a reviewer can name in one sentence.
scale.3: Architect. Meets the bar: complete, re-derivable, and the trade-off is stated.
scale.4: Principal. Exceeds the bar: the candidate tested the decision against its own reversal condition, or the evidence would convince a hostile reviewer.

anchors.1: An outcome exists but is a slogan; no non-goals or the kill criterion has no threshold.
anchors.2: Outcome and non-goals are concrete; the kill criterion is vague about how or when it is measured.
anchors.3: One-sentence outcome, at least two named non-goals, a kill criterion with a threshold and a measurement date.
anchors.4: As 3, and the kill criterion is wired to a metric the deployed system already emits.

anchors.0: No spec, or a PRD with no requirements.
anchors.1: Requirements exist without IDs or acceptance tests.
anchors.2: Requirements carry IDs; some trace to evals or ADRs; the NFR budget lacks numbers.
anchors.3: Every requirement has an ID and an acceptance eval or ADR; latency, cost and quality budgets are numeric.
anchors.4: As 3, and the spec is sized to the change: the candidate reports review time and cut sections that did not change a decision.

criteria.title: The four decisions are made or honestly open

anchors.1: Decisions described in prose with no verdict or evidence.
anchors.2: Model seam, loop shape, trust boundary and long-run home each have a verdict; some evidence pointers do not re-derive.
anchors.3: All four carry MADE or OPEN with a re-derivable evidence pointer; every OPEN has a dated deferral cost; all seven planes have an owner.
anchors.4: As 3, and the fix-first order among OPEN items is argued from reversal cost.

anchors.1: ADRs restate the chosen design; the alternatives are straw men.
anchors.2: At least three ADRs with real alternatives; reversal conditions are unobservable or missing in some.
anchors.3: At least three ADRs; each rejects an option a reasonable engineer would pick, names the cost being accepted, and states an observable reversal condition.
anchors.4: As 3, and at least one ADR records a reversal test that was actually run.

criteria.title: The model seam is proven on a second provider

anchors.0: Provider SDKs imported at call sites; no seam.
anchors.1: A seam is claimed but no eval ran through it on another provider.
anchors.2: An eval slice ran on a second provider or fake adapter; the gap report is missing quality, cost or latency.
anchors.3: Eval slice on a second provider with a gap report covering quality, cost and latency, and no product code changed above the seam.
anchors.4: As 3, and the failover path was exercised in the deployed system.

anchors.0: No diagram, or a picture with no model behind it.
anchors.1: One box-and-arrow diagram with unlabelled relationships.
anchors.2: Context and container views; the orchestrating container has no component view.
anchors.3: Context, container and an agent component view from one model file; every relationship says what crosses it.
anchors.4: As 3, and a deployment view maps containers to the two providers with the trust boundary drawn.

anchors.1: Agent elements tagged; tools, seam and human gates are not distinguished.
anchors.2: Profile tags present; some tool relationships lack a principal or side-effect flag.
anchors.3: Every Agent, Tool, ModelSeam, HumanGate and Untrusted element is tagged; every tool invocation names its principal and whether it has side effects.
anchors.4: As 3, and the diagram is generated or checked from the same authority matrix the code enforces.

anchors.1: A tool list without principals.
anchors.2: Principals per tool; a write principal is shared or a revocation path is missing.
anchors.3: Every tool flags side effects, no principal backs more than one side-effecting tool, every principal has a revocation path.
anchors.4: As 3, and the authority check runs outside the model and is covered by an eval.

anchors.1: Generic OWASP list with no link to this system.
anchors.2: System-specific, but tool or retrieval output is missing from untrusted inputs, or no risk is accepted.
anchors.3: Trust boundaries, untrusted inputs including tool results, abuse cases, mitigations, and named accepted risks.
anchors.4: As 3, and each abuse case maps to an eval case id.

anchors.1: An injection case exists but was never run.
anchors.2: It ran; it passes only because the model declined, with no check outside the model.
anchors.3: Injection cases from real untrusted sources run and fail closed through a deterministic guard.
anchors.4: As 3, plus an injection arriving through a tool result, not only through user input.

anchors.1: Happy-path cases only.
anchors.2: At least ten cases including refusal and injection; expectations a grader could decide two ways.
anchors.3: At least ten cases across golden, refusal, injection and edge kinds; each expect and must_not is decidable twice the same way.
anchors.4: As 3, and cases are drawn from production or realistic captured inputs with provenance.

anchors.1: A harness that has only ever reported green.
anchors.2: A seeded regression fails the harness, but fixtures change in the same commits as prompts.
anchors.3: A seeded regression makes the harness exit non-zero, and fixtures are versioned apart from the system under test.
anchors.4: As 3, and the harness gates deploys in CI.

anchors.0: No link between decisions and evals.
anchors.1: ADRs mention testing in general terms.
anchors.2: Some ADRs name an acceptance eval; some named cases do not exist.
anchors.3: Every ADR names acceptance eval ids that exist in the case set.
anchors.4: As 3, and the acceptance run is recorded with the ADR's status change.

criteria.title: Cost per unit of work from sourced prices

anchors.1: A monthly total with no unit.
anchors.2: Cost per unit; some price rows lack a source or are older than 90 days.
anchors.3: Cost per unit of work from price rows that each carry a source URL and a retrieval date within 90 days, plus a sensitivity band on three drivers.
anchors.4: As 3, and the unit cost is reconciled against observed usage from the deployed system.

anchors.1: A budget alert only.
anchors.2: A ceiling with an enforcing guard that has never been triggered.
anchors.3: A stated ceiling and a guard that stops spend, with evidence it fired in a test.
anchors.4: As 3, and the guard degrades the product visibly, with parked work and a reason the operator can see.

anchors.1: Deployed on one provider, or URLs that do not resolve for a stranger.
anchors.2: Two providers, but the split is incidental and undocumented.
anchors.3: Two distinct providers, each running a named plane, with live URLs and an ADR stating why the split exists.
anchors.4: As 3, and the same eval slice was run against the live deployment with results attached.

anchors.1: Prose runbook with no commands.
anchors.2: Commands present; rollback untested or no observability locator.
anchors.3: Rollback command per provider, observability locator, named owner, and a dry-run record.
anchors.4: As 3, and a rollback was executed and timed.

anchors.1: A story about an incident with no telemetry.
anchors.2: Injected failure detected, but by reading code or after the fact.
anchors.3: Injected failure mode named, detected by a signal that predates the injection, measured time to detection, a guard added, a witness attests.
anchors.4: As 3, and a replay of the original injection fails loudly on the new guard.

anchors.1: Cannot explain the submitted decisions.
anchors.2: Explains the decisions; changes the answer when pushed without new evidence.
anchors.3: Defends each ADR under a changed constraint and names what evidence would change the answer.
anchors.4: As 3, and identifies a weakness in the own submission the reviewers had not raised.

anchors.0: No attestation, or the work is not the candidate's.
anchors.1: Attestation signed; defence contradicts the commit history.
anchors.2: Attestation and disclosure present; disclosure is vague.
anchors.3: Signed attestation, specific AI-use disclosure, commit history spanning the work, defence consistent with both.
anchors.4: As 3, and the disclosure links the agent transcripts behind the two hardest decisions.
